subject: Approval needed: Multi-year price lock & uplift cap for NovoHealth
messages:
From: Jose Ramirez <j.ramirez@novohealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novohealth.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Multi-year pricing: request for price lock + uplift cap

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Procurement has a few commercial asks before we can move to legal:

- NovoHealth is asking for a 36-month price lock on the committed SKU (no more than a single annual uplift).
- An uplift cap (max percent increase) on published list prices for the locked SKUs — ideally <= 5%/yr.
- A renewal protection clause that guarantees preserved committed throughput and a step-down credit if Redwood materially changes unit economics.

Can you confirm if Redwood can provide written language and an initial price that reflects a 3-year commitment with these protections? We need rough numbers and a draft clause by EOD Friday (Dec 3) to keep our procurement window.

Thanks,
Jose
Jose Ramirez
Head of Procurement, NovoHealth
j.ramirez@novohealth.com

--
Attachment: NovoHealth_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 128KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jose Ramirez <j.ramirez@novohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing: request for price lock + uplift cap

Ben / David — looping you in. NovoHealth is pushing for a 36-month price lock + uplift cap (they proposed <=5%/yr) and renewal protection language. Rough commercials below:

- Term: 36 months committed (annual invoicing).
- Proposed list discount: 18% on committed units (year 1), step to 14% if commitment not met.
- Price lock: hold per-unit price for 36 months; only one scheduled annual uplift allowed under the cap.
- Suggested uplift cap: 6% max annually (my ask: we consider 6% vs their 5%).

Attached: "NovoHealth_Renewal_Protection_Summary.docx" and a quick calc "price_calc_nov2026.xlsx".

Business notes: NovoHealth is regional (US) health SaaS — potential to expand to 3 additional product lines in year 2. If we lose this, likely move to competitor X who offered a shallower discount but no long price lock. Win has strategic value.

Can you confirm willingness to approve: (A) 36-month price lock; (B) uplift cap at 6% annual; (C) renewal protection language limited to credits (no guaranteed future pricing) — and whether we need an exec sign-off for the 18% discount? I can draft the clause and route to Legal.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0192

--
Attachments: NovoHealth_Renewal_Protection_Summary.docx, price_calc_nov2026.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing: request for price lock + uplift cap

+1 on moving quickly here. A few notes:

- 36-month price lock is acceptable provided we limit the definition to the committed SKU and exclude significant product re-architects or major feature bundles.
- I prefer an uplift cap at 8% rather than 6% given inflation and GPU market volatility; 6% would be a potential margin hit if spot pricing spikes.
- Renewal protection: keep it to a credit mechanism capped at X% of ARR (I put a placeholder in the attached calc). No forward pricing guarantees.

If David / Marissa are comfortable with an exception for the 18% first-year discount (with staged ramp), I recommend we proceed with Legal to draft the clause and a short-side rider for exceptions.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Mid-Market Sales
ben_carter@redwood.com

--
Attachment referenced: price_calc_nov2026.xlsx (updated with uplift scenarios)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jose Ramirez <j.ramirez@novohealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: Exec approval request — 36m price lock & 18% first-year discount for NovoHealth (RDW-DEAL-2026-091)

Marissa — short ask: can I get executive sign-off to approve a commercial exception for NovoHealth? Summary here; full thread below.

Why this matters:
- Strategic expansion: NovoHealth is the lead for a regional health network; contract includes an option to expand to 3 additional product SKUs in year 2 (material upside).
- Competitive timing: Procurement has a tight vendor window and is explicit they're choosing a vendor by Dec 10.
- Revenue predictability: Contract is a 36-month committed ARR with predictable monthly billings; our downside is limited to short-term margin pressure.

Requested exceptions / protections:
1) Approve 18% discount on committed units for year 1 (staged to 14% in year 2+ if thresholds not met).
2) Accept a 36-month price lock on committed SKU(s) with an annual uplift cap at 6% (Ben prefers 8% but we propose 6% to close deal).
3) Renewal protection to be implemented as a credit mechanism (cap credit at 10% of first-year ARR), no guaranteed future pricing.

Risk mitigations included: staged ramp targets, credit caps, carve-outs for materially new product features, and Legal sign-off required on final wording. Attachments: SOW, pricing calc, and draft clause.

If approved I will instruct Legal to finalize the clause and I will route to Procurement + DocuSign. If you want an alternate uplift cap (8%) I need sign-off today to keep to NovoHealth timeline.

Best,
David
David Kim
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

--
